subtitle: In Mandu, three scripts carry one restless age of learning

panels.shot: wide, low-angle twilight view of Mandu’s Ashrafi Mahal and Jami Masjid with Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts in the foreground holding palm-leaf and paper
panels.action: Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts stands between the looming silhouette of the Ashrafi Mahal madrasa and the great Jami Masjid, holding a palm-leaf manuscript in one hand and a Persian paper codex in the other, as the Malwa plateau stretches behind him.

dialogue.text: In Mandu’s wind, stone inscriptions praise a madrasa, while Jain colophons whisper from faraway libraries—how did one small plateau feed so many tongues of learning?

i18n.hi: मांडू की हवा में पत्थर मदरसे की वाहवाही करें, और दूर की लाइब्रेरी से जैन टिप्पणी फुसफुसाए—कैसे इस छोटे पठार ने इतनी भाषाओं को जगा रखा?

panels.shot: slow push-in from bird’s-eye over Mandu’s plateau to the clustered complex of the Jami Masjid and Ashrafi Mahal
panels.action: From high above the rocky Malwa plateau, the camera descends toward the massive courtyard of the Jami Masjid and the tiered ruins of the Ashrafi Mahal, where Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts walks as a small figure between stone arcades.

dialogue.text: By the early 1400s, Mandu had become the proud hill-capital of the Malwa sultans, its heart beating between a great Friday mosque and a new madrasa rising beside it.

i18n.hi: चौदहवीं सदी की शुरुआत तक मांडू मलवा सुल्तानों की शान बन चुका था, दिल में जामा मस्जिद और उसके पास उठती नई मदरसा।

panels.shot: medium close-up of a carved Persian inscription slab on Ashrafi Mahal, with the scholar’s hand tracing the letters
panels.action: Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts, in simple robes, gently runs his fingers over a carved Persian inscription panel set into the Ashrafi Mahal wall, his eyes intent on the elegant Nastaliq letters.

dialogue.text: On these stones, Persian words fix the sultans’ names and their gifts: a madrasa for Islamic law and theology, public proof that Malwa’s rulers now spoke in a Persianate tongue of power.

i18n.hi: इन पत्थरों पर फ़ारसी में खुदे हैं सुल्तानों के नाम और उनके इनाम: क़ानून और कलाम की मदरसा, खुला ऐलान कि मलवा अब फ़ारसी ज़बान में हुक्म चलाता है।

panels.shot: interior wide of the Ashrafi Mahal madrasa courtyard, students in small groups with books, arches framing the Jami Masjid beyond
panels.action: Inside the Ashrafi Mahal courtyard, Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts sits among rows of students and teachers under arcades, some reciting from Persian paper codices, while the domes of the Jami Masjid rise beyond the arches.

dialogue.text: Here, young men bend over paper codices, learning Qur’an, hadith, law and language, their voices weaving with the call to prayer from the Jami Masjid just across the courtyard.

i18n.hi: यहीं नौजवान काग़ज़ी किताबों पर झुके, कुरान, हदीस, फ़िक़्ह और ज़बान पढ़ते, उनकी आवाज़ें आँगन पार जामे मस्जिद की अज़ान में घुलतीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of the scholar at a low desk, alternating between Persian script and another script on palm leaf
panels.action: Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts sits at a low desk in a small cell, one side stacked with Persian paper books, the other with palm-leaf manuscripts, as he writes first in Persian on paper and then in a different script on a leaf.

dialogue.text: Mandu’s court life turns on Persian, yet the scholar’s hand does not know only one path; in quiet corners, older scripts and palm leaves still claim time and care.

i18n.hi: दरबार में ज़ुबान फ़ारसी, पर उस्ताद का हाथ सिर्फ एक राह नहीं जानता; कोनों में पुरानी लिपियाँ और ताड़पत्र अभी भी वक़्त और निगाह माँगते हैं।

panels.shot: cutaway wide of old ruins at Dhar in the distance, overlaid with a subtle dissolve back to the Ashrafi Mahal
panels.action: The image shows weathered pillars of an older temple-complex at Dhar in soft focus, then dissolves back to the Ashrafi Mahal, where Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts looks toward the horizon as if seeing the past.

dialogue.text: A century earlier, Paramara kings at Dhar had made their name with Sanskrit learning, but under the sultans that old courtly world faded; the new state wrote itself instead in Persian.

i18n.hi: सदी भर पहले, धार के परमार राजाओं ने संस्कृत विद्या से नाम कमाया था, पर सुल्तानों के साथ वह दरबारी दुनिया ढल गई; अब नई हुकूमत अपना किस्सा फ़ारसी में लिखती है।

panels.shot: intimate interior of a Jain temple-library in a Malwa town, lit by lamps, with the scholar visiting respectfully
panels.action: In a modest Jain temple-library within a Malwa town, rows of palm-leaf bundles rest on wooden racks, while Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts stands respectfully near a seated Jain scribe preparing ink and stylus by lamplight.

dialogue.text: Yet beyond the hill-fort, Jain communities quietly keep another flame, copying Sanskrit and Prakrit texts for their own temples and schools, apart from the sultan’s court.

i18n.hi: पर किले की ढलानों के नीचे, जैन समाज चुपचाप दूसरी लौ संभाले, अपने मंदिरों और पाठशालाओं के लिए संस्कृत–प्राकृत ग्रंथ नकल करते रहते हैं, दरबार से अलग।

panels.shot: close-up of a Jain scribe’s hands tying a manuscript bundle, with the scholar watching and a tiny colophon visible at the edge
panels.action: A Jain scribe’s careful hands wrap a string around a palm-leaf manuscript bundle, while Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts watches; at the leaf’s edge, fine script forms a small colophon line noting date and place.

dialogue.text: In their colophons—single, spare lines at the end of a text—they note who copied it, for whom, when, and often from where in Malwa the manuscript began its journey.

i18n.hi: उनके कोलोफ़न—ग्रंथ के अंत में एक सादी पंक्ति—बताते हैं किसने लिखा, किसके लिए, कब, और मलवा के किस गाँव या नगर से यह पांडुलिपि चली थी।

panels.shot: map-like overhead montage, with hand-drawn lines connecting Malwa towns to Patan, Jaisalmer and Ahmedabad, the scholar’s hand pointing
panels.action: From above, a textured map of western India shows Mandu and Malwa towns, with faint lines stretching to Patan, Jaisalmer and Ahmedabad as Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts’ hand hovers over these routes.

dialogue.text: Those tiny notes, now read in libraries at Patan, Jaisalmer and Ahmedabad, reveal a web: texts copied in Malwa, then carried along merchant and monastic routes to western India.

i18n.hi: आज पाटण, जैसलमेर और अहमदाबाद की लाइब्रेरी में पढ़ी जाती वही छोटी टिप्पणियाँ बताती हैं जाल: ग्रंथ मलवा में नकल हुए, फिर व्यापारी और साधु मार्गों से पश्चिमी भारत तक चले।

panels.shot: split-panel style composition: on one side the madrasa class; on the other a Jain copying hall, the scholar’s figure overlapping both
panels.action: The frame divides vertically, with Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts straddling the split; on the left, he sits among Persian-using madrasa students in Mandu, and on the right, he kneels near Jain copyists bent over palm leaves.

dialogue.text: These worlds overlap in time but not in rank; the madrasa is tied to the sultan’s treasury and law, the Jain library to merchant guilds and community vows, each guarding its own habits and hopes.

i18n.hi: ये दुनिया समय में साथ हैं, दर्जे में नहीं; मदरसा सुल्तान के ख़ज़ाने और क़ानून से बंधा, जैन पुस्तकालय व्यापारी संघों और समाजी व्रतों से, दोनों अपनी अपनी आदतें और उम्मीदें बचाए।

panels.shot: medium shot in the madrasa, a teacher gesturing to a Persian legal text as the scholar listens
panels.action: Inside a madrasa hall, a bearded teacher gestures to a Persian legal text spread before him, his students attentive, while Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts listens, his fingers resting thoughtfully on the margin.

dialogue.text: Here, jurists debate contracts, taxes and endowments, equipping a class of scholars who can run courts, draft orders and anchor Malwa’s place in the wider Persianate world.

i18n.hi: यहीं फ़क़ीह सौदों, करों और वक़्फ़ पर बहस करें, ऐसे आलिम तैयार करते जो अदालतें चला सकें, फ़रमान लिख सकें और मलवा को बड़े फ़ारसी जहाँ से जोड़ सकें।

panels.shot: medium shot in the Jain library, a monk pointing to a passage on a palm leaf while the scholar observes quietly
panels.action: In the Jain library, a calm monk in white indicates a verse on a palm leaf to a younger disciple, as Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts watches from the side, hands folded, not intruding.

dialogue.text: In Jain halls, teachers explain logic, ethics and cosmology, less concerned with the court than with monastic rules, pilgrimage routes and the merit of copying a single difficult text correctly.

i18n.hi: जैन सभाओं में आचार्य तर्क, नीति और जगत की रचना समझाएँ, दरबार से कम, मठों के नियम, तीर्थ–यात्राएँ और एक कठिन ग्रंथ को ठीक से नकल करने के पुण्य से ज़्यादा मतलब।

panels.shot: night interior of the madrasa rooftop, the scholar copying a Persian inscription by lamplight with the mosque courtyard below
panels.action: At night on an upper terrace of the Ashrafi Mahal, Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts copies lines from a Persian inscription onto paper by lamplight, the darkened Jami Masjid courtyard spreading below him.

dialogue.text: The inscriptions at Mandu fix a certain face of knowledge in stone: a Persianate Malwa that honors patrons, piety and the training of jurists, each letter part of the architecture of rule.

i18n.hi: मांडू की शिलालेख विद्या का एक चेहरा पत्थर पर जमा देते हैं: फ़ारसी-मय मलवा, जहाँ सरपरस्त, भक्ति और क़ाज़ियों की तालीम का मान, हर अक्षर खुद इमारत का हिस्सा।

panels.shot: contrasting close-up of an old Jain manuscript colophon being read in a western Indian library, with the scholar’s imagined silhouette faintly overlaid
panels.action: In a later western Indian library, a present-day hand gently opens an old Jain manuscript, revealing a colophon naming a Malwa town, while the faint, ghostly silhouette of Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts appears behind the leaves.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, scholars reading these colophons piece together another map: one where Jain scribes in Malwa kept copying amid political change, their names preserved only in these final lines.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, ये कोलोफ़न पढ़ते विद्वान दूसरी नक़्शा जोड़ते हैं: जहाँ मलवा के जैन लेखक सत्ता बदलते देख भी नकल करते रहे, उनके नाम बस इन आख़िरी पंक्तियों में बचे।

panels.shot: wide shot of Mandu’s skyline under changing light, from Mahmud Khalji’s time to Bahadur Shah’s conquest, with subtle dissolves
panels.action: The skyline of Mandu shifts through a dissolving montage—from the bustling age of Mahmud Khalji to the quieter years before Bahadur Shah’s conquest—while Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts walks along the ramparts, now older.

dialogue.text: Between roughly 1405 and 1531, sultans rose and fell, armies marched and alliances turned, yet the streams of learning in Mandu did not simply vanish; they bent, narrowed or flowed into new channels.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1405 से 1531 तक सुल्तान उठे–गिरे, फ़ौजें चलीं, गठजोड़ पलटे, पर मांडू की विद्या की धारियाँ ग़ायब नहीं हुईं; बस मुड़ीं, पतली हुईं या नई राहों में चुपके से बह गईं।

panels.shot: low-angle view of the scholar standing between a mosque doorway and a caravan road leading toward the west
panels.action: Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts stands with one shoulder near the grand doorway of the Jami Masjid and the other facing a dusty road where a caravan heads westward, carrying cloth bundles of manuscripts.

dialogue.speaker: mandu_s_scholars_and_scribes
dialogue.text: Words may serve courts or communities; the road remembers both.

i18n.hi: लफ़्ज़ कभी दरबार की ख़िदमत, कभी समाज की; सड़क दोनों की याद रखती है।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot inside a ruined Ashrafi Mahal classroom, with Persian carvings and a lone palm-leaf resting on the floor
panels.action: In the quiet ruin of an Ashrafi Mahal classroom, Persian inscriptions still cling to the walls, while a single palm leaf lies on the dusty floor beside a crumbled niche, and Mandu’s Scholar of Many Scripts sits cross-legged, gazing at both.

dialogue.text: Mandu’s story reminds us that a region’s memory rarely speaks in just one script; it survives in stone and leaf, mosque and monastery, Persian decree and Jain colophon, all sharing the same restless sky.

i18n.hi: मांडू की कहानी बताती है कि किसी इलाक़े की याद एक ही लिपि में नहीं बोलती; वह पत्थर और पत्तों में, मस्जिद और मठ में, फ़ारसी फ़रमान और जैन टिप्पणी में, एक ही बेचैन आसमान बाँटकर जीवित रहती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: In Mandu, three scripts carry one restless age of learning
subtitle_i18n.hi: मांडू में तीन लिपियाँ, एक बेचैन दौर की कहानी
